title: A wrapper-opened claim records the runner's process identity, so reattach can match it
description:
DAEMON HALF of task-5e096de9, split out by its architect on 2026-09-18 (the card itself asked for a SPIDR split; the whole thing was ~10 files, the plan-size ceiling). That card keeps the runner half: both wrappers capture the identity, send it at claim, and reattach when the heartbeat asks them to.

THE GAP THIS CARD CLOSES. moe.reattach_attempt (task-d7fa98f4) matches an attempt on attemptId + generation + processStartedAt + host, and refuses an attempt that recorded none: reattachAttempt.ts identityMismatch answers 'processStartedAt (none recorded)'. But openClaimAttempt (tools/claimNextTask.ts ~69-76) opens every real attempt with only taskId, workerId, runnerId=workerId and workspace — its own comment says "A distinct runner identity and a per-attempt workspace arrive with the reattachment work". attemptStore.openAttempt ALREADY persists params.processStartedAt and params.host when they are supplied, so nothing in the store needs changing. claim_next_task simply never offers them, so no production attempt can ever be reattached, and Wave 1 acceptance case 4 passes only because its fixture writes those two fields into the record itself and then plays the runner (acceptance.test.ts ~1690-1718).

SCOPE
- claim_next_task accepts optional `processStartedAt` and `host` (and keeps working exactly as today when they are absent — every non-wrapper caller, the plugin board and older wrappers included).
- They are validated as opaque bounded strings and passed through openClaimAttempt to openAttempt. The daemon never probes a process and never derives either value: the runner supplies them, or they are absent.
- The adopt arm of a resume keeps the identity the attempt already carries; a claim never rewrites it.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md claim_next_task and reattach_attempt describe the pair.

NOT IN SCOPE: the wrappers, the harnesses, parity, and any change to the reconcile-window give-up. All of those stay with task-5e096de9.
definitionOfDone: claim_next_task accepts optional processStartedAt and host, validates them as bounded non-blank strings, and openClaimAttempt passes them to openAttempt so the opened attempt carries both; a claim that omits them behaves byte-for-byte as today

A daemon test claims through the real tool with an identity, simulates a daemon-only restart (fresh StateManager, load, reconcileRunningAttempts, purgeAllWorkers), and moe.reattach_attempt with that same identity is ACCEPTED and returns the attempt to running - with no fixture-seeded attempt record anywhere in the test
A mismatched processStartedAt or host is still refused with ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH before any write, and an attempt that recorded no identity is still unmatchable
The reconcile-window give-up is unchanged: an attempt that never reattaches is still released after reconcileWindowMs, proven by a test
docs/MCP_SERVER.md describes the identity pair on claim_next_task and how reattach_attempt compares it; packages/moe-daemon npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass
taskRails: The daemon stays state-only: process identity is supplied by the runner, never probed or derived by the daemon.
Both values stay optional; a caller that omits them must be unaffected.
Do not weaken the give-up for seats that never reattach, and add no idle-based release.

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 1+2 — re-read the four anchors and record baselines. No repo edits.

Verified in source while planning; confirm each still holds by grep, never by line number:
- `attemptStore.OpenAttemptParams` ALREADY carries optional `processStartedAt` and `host`, and `openAttempt` spreads them onto the record when they are defined. Nothing in the store changes in this card.
- `openClaimAttempt` (tools/claimNextTask.ts) builds its params as `{ taskId, workerId, runnerId: workerId, workspace: state.projectPath }` with a comment saying a distinct runner identity "arrives with the reattachment work". That is this card. Its single call site is in the claim handler.
- `reattachAttempt.identityMismatch` compares generation, then processStartedAt, then host, as EXACT strings, and answers 'processStartedAt (none recorded)' for an attempt that carries none. It deliberately does not compare workerId or runnerId.
- `runReconcileWindowSweep` takes an injectable `nowMs`, so the give-up is testable without waiting.

Also record, so step 2 does not duplicate cover and step 5 can prove nothing weakened:
- The existing give-up test in state/sweeps.test.ts (name it exactly) that proves a reconciling attempt past reconcileWindowMs is closed and its row released.
- The existing reattach tests in tools/reattachAttempt.test.ts, in particular the ones that seed a record with `seedReconciling`/`openAttempt`. The new integration case in step 2 may NOT use those helpers — DoD 2 requires an attempt that a real claim opened.
- Wave 1 acceptance case 4 seeds the identity into the record itself and plays the runner; it must keep passing untouched.

Baselines with counts: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 3 — tests first. Two files, both red before step 3.

(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts — the pass-through and the tolerances:
- A claim carrying processStartedAt and host opens an attempt whose RECORD ON DISK holds both, byte-compared against what was sent (read the .moe/attempts/<id>.json file, not the in-memory copy).
- A claim that omits them opens an attempt with neither key present, and the rest of the record is byte-identical to today's — that is the 'unaffected caller' rail, and a test that only checks `undefined` would not catch a key written as null.
- Each value is validated: blank, non-string, control characters, and over-length are refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the field, BEFORE any assignment write (spy on state.updateTask, or compare the task file bytes) so a refused claim leaves the board untouched.
- One value without the other is refused the same way: a half identity records something no later reattach can reproduce.
- The adopt arm (a resume that finds its own open attempt) NEVER rewrites the identity already on the record, even when the claim presents different values.

(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reattachAttempt.test.ts — a new describe for the restart path. It may not call openAttempt or seedReconciling; every attempt in it comes from the real claim tool:
- Claim a WORKING row through claimNextTaskTool with an identity, then simulate a daemon-only restart: clearEmitter on the old state, `new StateManager({ projectPath: h.testDir })`, `load()`, `reconcileRunningAttempts`, `purgeAllWorkers()` (the seat is spared because it holds an open attempt — do not assert the record is gone).
- The attempt is now `reconciling` and the row is still assigned. moe.reattach_attempt with the SAME identity is accepted, the attempt is `running`, and the task and worker records are byte-identical to before the call.
- Then `runReconcileWindowSweep(state, now + reconcileWindowMs + 1)` releases NOTHING: the row stays assigned, because a reattached attempt is no longer reconciling.
- A mismatched processStartedAt, and separately a mismatched host, are still refused with ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH and leave the attempt reconciling.
- A claim that recorded no identity produces an attempt the same restart leaves unmatchable, refused with 'processStartedAt (none recorded)'.
- A seat that never reattaches is STILL given up: after the same clock push, that attempt is closed and its row released — the give-up this card must not weaken.

Run both files before touching claimNextTask.ts and record the failures: the pass-through cases fail because the schema rejects the unknown properties (additionalProperties is false), and the restart case fails at the reattach with 'processStartedAt (none recorded)'. Those two messages are the red proof.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4 — the implementation, in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts only.

- Input schema: add `processStartedAt` and `host` as optional strings beside workerId, each with a description saying the runner supplies it, the daemon never derives it, and reattach compares it as an exact string. `additionalProperties` stays false.
- Handler params: read both, then validate with the file's existing error helpers — non-blank after trim, no control characters, and a bound (255 for host, matching the receipt target's bound; 200 for the start time, which is a timestamp or a `<pid>@<token>` pair, never prose). Refuse with INVALID_INPUT naming the field. Refuse a half identity (one supplied without the other) the same way.
- Refusing rather than silently dropping is the deliberate choice: a dropped value looks like success and costs the seat its reattachability hours later, at a restart, with nothing in the log. Every other validated input in this slice refuses too (record_delivery_receipt refuses an over-long pushResult rather than truncating it). Say so in a comment.
- Thread the pair into `openClaimAttempt` as an optional identity argument and into the `openAttempt` params it builds, replacing the 'arrives with the reattachment work' comment with what actually arrived. Nothing else in that function changes: its three arms, its refusals and its ordering stay exactly as they are.
- The adopt arm returns the existing attempt untouched, so the identity on a resumed attempt is whatever its opening claim recorded. openAttempt's repair path already refuses to adopt different params; do not add a second rule.

Error handling: validation throws before the claim does any work, so a refused claim writes nothing and assigns nobody. A claim that omits the pair takes exactly today's path — no new branch, no new field on the record.

Both test files from step 2 turn green.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 5 — regression and mutation proof, from packages/moe-daemon.

(a) `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit`. The only count that may move is the two test files this card adds cases to. Anything else moving means the change reached further than the claim path.

(b) Mutation replay in a scratch tree (mem:pattern-red-proof-by-scratch-tree-mutation-vitest), one site at a time, restoring from pristine before each, with an unmutated run first and last:
- Drop the pair from the openClaimAttempt params: the restart case goes red at the reattach, with 'processStartedAt (none recorded)'.
- Keep the pass-through but skip validation: the blank, control-character, over-length and half-identity cases go red.
- Let the adopt arm overwrite the identity: the resume case goes red.
- Record the identity but hand reattach a recomputed value instead of the stored one: the exact-string case goes red — this pins that the comparison is on the recorded value, not on a re-derivation.
- Widen the sweep to skip running attempts it should still close: the give-up case goes red, proving that test bites.
Each failure must be behavioural, not a missing symbol.

(c) Confirm the two suites this card must not disturb: `npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` (case 4 still passes with its own seeded identity) and `npx vitest run src/state/sweeps.test.ts`.

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 7+8 — adversarial self-review, then complete. Answer in ONE task comment:
1. The daemon derives nothing: show that both values arrive from the caller and that no code path probes a process, reads a clock for them or fills a default (task rail 1).
2. Optional means unaffected: a claim without the pair writes a record byte-identical to today's. Say how the test proves it (file bytes, not an undefined check).
3. Half identity: why it is refused rather than half-recorded, and why refusing beats silently dropping a malformed value.
4. Adoption: a resumed attempt keeps the identity its opening claim recorded, and openAttempt's repair path already refuses to adopt different params — confirm there is exactly one rule, not two.
5. The give-up is intact: name the test that proves a seat which never reattaches is still released after reconcileWindowMs, and confirm no idle signal entered any path here (task rail 3).
6. What this card does NOT deliver: no wrapper sends the pair yet, so the fleet still cannot reattach. Name task-5e096de9 and say the change is inert until it lands — and that it only takes effect after a daemon rebuild and restart.
7. Would I be embarrassed if this broke in production? Name the worst case — a claim refused over a malformed identity would stop a seat entirely — and say which test covers it.

Then: delete any scratch tree (unlink junctions first), cmp the repo sources against your final copies to prove no mutant leaked, call moe.declare_files for exactly the four files this plan names, and moe.complete_task with verification `{ command: 'cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test', exitCode: 0, outputTail }` plus a summary naming the new cases, the mutation results and whether docs/MCP_SERVER.md landed or was skipped as contested.

comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (step 6), read off `git diff packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts`.

1. THE DAEMON DERIVES NOTHING. Both values enter as `params.processStartedAt` / `params.host`, typed `unknown`, and leave `readProcessIdentity` as the same strings — no `Date`, no `os.hostname()`, no `process.*`, no default, no normalisation, no fallback. The only helper they touch (`readIdentityField`) refuses or returns `value` unchanged. `openClaimAttempt` spreads them into the openAttempt params, and `attemptStore.openAttempt` persists them only when defined (its code is untouched by this card). Nothing reads them back except `reattachAttempt.identityMismatch`, which compares strings. Mutation evidence that recording is verbatim: `lowercase-host` (recompute the recorded host) turns 'records the identity on the attempt file exactly as the claim sent it' and the resume case red; `normalise-recorded` turns the exact-string case red behaviourally ('expected a MoeError refusal, but the reattach resolved'). No code path probes a process or reads a clock for these values.

2. OPTIONAL MEANS UNAFFECTED. `readProcessIdentity` returns `null` when BOTH are `undefined`, and `...null` spreads to nothing, so the params object openAttempt receives is the object it received before this card — no new branch in the claim path, no new key on the record. The test does not check for `undefined`: 'writes a claim that sends no identity byte for byte as before: no key, not even a null one' compares the WHOLE attempt file text against `JSON.stringify({id, taskId, workerId, runnerId, generation, workspace, phase, startedAt, lastPhaseAt}, null, 2)` — key set, key order and bytes. The `null-keys` mutant (write the two keys as null when absent) turns exactly that case red, plus the adopt-{} case and the restart no-identity case.

3. HALF IDENTITY. reattach compares processStartedAt AND host, both exactly, and refuses an attempt missing either; so recording one alone stores something no reattach could ever reproduce — a seat that believes it is reattachable and is not. Refusing beats dropping for the same reason the card states and `record_delivery_receipt` already follows: a dropped value returns `hasNext: true`, looks like a perfectly good claim, and the cost surfaces hours later at a restart with nothing in the log to explain it — while a refusal surfaces in the wrapper's own launch, immediately, naming the field. The refusal names the MISSING half and says 'must be supplied together with <the other>': I found during mutation that asserting only `context.field` did NOT pin those two branches (readIdentityField refuses the undefined half with the same field), so the test now asserts the message text — `MoeError.context` does not cross the MCP wire, so the both-or-neither rule has to be in the words a runner reads. `drop-half-checks` turns exactly those 2 cases red.

4. ADOPTION — ONE RULE, NOT TWO. `openClaimAttempt` arm 2 still returns the open attempt untouched; I added no identity handling there. A resumed attempt therefore carries whatever its opening claim recorded, and a resuming claim presenting different values changes nothing on disk (test: 'a resume by the holder keeps … whatever the resuming claim presents', asserted on file bytes + the identity keys, for both an identity-bearing and an identity-less opening claim; `adopt-overwrite` turns both red). The store's own repair path (`repairExisting`) still refuses to adopt a caller's other params; I did not add a second rule in the tool, so "the opening claim's values win" is stated once, in the store, and simply not contradicted here.

5. THE GIVE-UP IS INTACT. New test: 'still gives up a seat that never reattaches: the window closes its attempt and releases the row' (reattachAttempt.test.ts, restart describe) — a real claim WITH an identity, a real restart, then `checkReconcileWindow(state, now + reconcileWindowMs + 1)` closes the attempt and releases the row to WORKING-unassigned. The pre-existing 'closes a reconciling attempt past the window and releases its task' (sweeps.test.ts) is untouched and still passes. `sweep-skips-identity` (the plausible wrong "an attempt with an identity can still reattach, give it more time") turns the new case red — the test bites. No idle signal entered any path: this card adds no read of `lastActivityAt`, no presence check, no timer; `sweeps.ts` and `attemptStore.ts` are not modified at all.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DELIVER. No wrapper sends the pair yet, so no seat in the fleet becomes reattachable from this card alone. The runner half is task-5e096de9 (both wrappers compute `<pid>@<start token>` + host once at wrapper start, send them at claim, and call `moe.reattach_attempt` when `moe.heartbeat` answers `reattachRequired`). Until that lands the change is inert — and even then only after the daemon is REBUILT (`npm run build`) and RESTARTED, since the live daemon runs `dist/`. docs/MCP_SERVER.md says this in both sections so no reader concludes the fleet reattaches today.

7. EMBARRASSMENT TEST. Worst case: a wrapper computes a malformed value (an empty `ps` result, a hostname with a stray newline), sends it on every claim, and every claim of that seat is refused with INVALID_INPUT — the seat stops entirely rather than working without reattachability. That is the deliberate trade in (3), it is loud and immediate rather than silent, the bounds are generous (200/255 against realistic values of ~40 and ~253), and the runner half's own rule is to send NEITHER value when either is unavailable. Covered by the 8 refusal rows + 2 half-identity rows in claimNextTask.test.ts, and by 'refuses a %s that is %s with INVALID_INPUT, before any write', which also proves the refusal costs the board nothing (updateTask and writeEntity spies not called, task file bytes unchanged, no attempt, no worker record). Two more findings from the same pass: (a) FIXED IN THIS STEP — the control-character scan walked the whole string BEFORE the length bound, so a caller sending megabytes would have been scanned (and `trim()`-copied) inside the global state mutex, freezing every other tool fleet-wide; the checks are now typeof → length → blank → control scan, all O(1) before anything walks the value. Behaviour is unchanged (same field named for every case), so no test pins the order — it is defensive. (b) NOTED, not changed: a claim that names no `workerId` opens no attempt, yet its identity is still validated and then discarded; refusing malformed input regardless of whether it would have been used is the conservative direction, and accepting it silently for that caller would make the contract caller-dependent. Also confirmed: nothing else calls `openClaimAttempt` (single call site), the identity is never used in a path, a command or a log format string, and the values are not secrets — a match narrows WHICH process, it never authenticates one, exactly as reattach_attempt's docs already say.

COMMIT: completion f8ecb8e on moe/work-2026-09-13 (pushed, 5 paths): claimNextTask.ts +72/-7, claimNextTask.test.ts +159, reattachAttempt.test.ts +162/-2, docs/MCP_SERVER.md +7/-1 (the contested doc landed). attemptStore.ts and sweeps.ts are unchanged. RE-RUN on a clean `git archive HEAD` export (65bfc97, node_modules junctioned), so peers' dirty files could not skew it: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npm test` exit 0, 122 files, 2103 passed | 2 skipped. The 2 skips are other owners' `it.skip` acceptance cases that are already at HEAD (generation-N fencing, crash-before-receipt). The worker's 2105/1 came from the shared tree, where a peer's in-flight acceptance.test.ts un-skips one of them. Per-file counts: claimNextTask.test 62, reattachAttempt.test 26. Acceptance case 4 ('restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership') passes. In the shared tree, claimNextTask/reattachAttempt/sweeps/acceptance ran 4 files, 103 passed | 1 skipped.

DoD:
(1) The pair is in the schema (additionalProperties still false). readProcessIdentity runs right after the statuses check. The bounds are 200 and 255. INVALID_INPUT (-32602) names the field. An omitted pair spreads nothing, and the test byte-compares the whole attempt file.
(2) The restart describe opens every attempt through the real claimNextTaskTool (no openAttempt/seedReconciling). The restart runs fresh StateManager, load, runExclusive(reconcileRunningAttempts), purgeAllWorkers, which is the same order as index.ts:501-507.
(3) A mismatch is refused with ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH and leaves the attempt bytes unchanged. A claim sent with no identity stays unmatchable.
(4) checkReconcileWindow, the production mutex entry point, still closes the attempt and releases the row.
(5) The docs cover both tools and name task-5e096de9.

MUTATION REPLAY in scratch (restored before each run; unmutated 88/88 first, 98/98 last):
- claimNextTask.ts reverted to f8ecb8e^: 17 red. The restart case fails with '(processStartedAt (none recorded) differs)'.
- Half identity silently dropped: 2 red.
- Length bound removed: 2 red.
- Sweep spares identity-bearing attempts: 1 red, and ONLY the new give-up test catches it. The 10 existing sweeps tests do not.
- Adopt arm rewrites the identity on disk: 2 red.
- Validation moved after the assignment write: 10 red ('updateTask called 2 times').

RAILS: the diff has no os/hostname/process/Date use for the identity. No idle signal was added. No forbidden patterns. McpAdapter does not validate inputSchema, so the schema entries are for discovery only; the handler is the enforcement point, and it is tested.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
This is the daemon half of the reattach split (task-5e096de9, comment-c14c7609); the human approved the split in the architect REPL. The runner half owns both wrappers, the harnesses, parity and the restart story in CLAUDE.md.

- The store needs no change: OpenAttemptParams already carries the optional pair and openAttempt already persists it. The only gap is that claim_next_task never offers it.
- A supplied-but-malformed value is REFUSED, not dropped. A dropped value reads as success and costs the seat its reattachability hours later at a restart, with nothing in the log; every other validated input in this slice refuses too.
- Both or neither: a half identity records something no later reattach can reproduce, since the daemon compares both fields exactly.
- The adopt arm keeps whatever identity the opening claim recorded. openAttempt's repair path already refuses to adopt different params, so adding a second rule here would be two sources of truth.
- Rejected: making the pair required (every non-wrapper caller — the plugin board, moe-call.sh, older wrappers — would break, and the rail says optional). Rejected: having the daemon fill a default or probe the process (task rail 1). Rejected: rewriting the identity on every claim of an existing attempt, which would let a second process adopt a live execution by claiming.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- tools/claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt builds `{ taskId, workerId, runnerId: workerId, workspace }` and its comment says the runner identity 'arrives with the reattachment work'. One call site, inside the handler's exclusive block.
- reattachAttempt compares generation, processStartedAt and host as exact strings and answers 'processStartedAt (none recorded)' when the attempt has none — which is why no production attempt has ever been reattachable.
- runReconcileWindowSweep takes an injectable nowMs, closes the attempt BEFORE releasing the row, and releases only the seat that attempt held — so the give-up is easy to test without waiting and hard to weaken by accident.
- The existing reattach tests seed their attempts with openAttempt/seedReconciling, which is exactly what DoD 2 forbids for the new case: it must come from a real claim.
- purgeAllWorkers spares a seat that holds an open attempt, so the restart simulation must not assert the worker record is gone (mem:gotcha-backstop-masks-untested-prewrite-guard).
- Wave 1 acceptance case 4 seeds the identity itself and plays the runner; it keeps passing untouched.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A validation that is too strict refuses claims and stops seats; the bounds are deliberately generous (255 for host, 200 for the start time) and the wrapper's own rule is to send neither value when either is unavailable.
2. claim_next_task is the hottest tool on the board. The change must add no branch to the path a caller without the pair takes, and the test asserts that on file bytes.
3. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is contested in this epic and has been skipped by a landing before; verify it reached task.commits.
4. The change is inert until the runner half (task-5e096de9) lands AND the daemon is rebuilt and restarted. Say so in the completion summary so nobody reads this card as fixing the fleet.
5. Do not touch the reconcile-window give-up or add any idle signal; the mutation series includes a sweep mutant precisely to prove that test still bites.
